title: Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial of a Transdiagnostic, Modular Intervention for Youth at Risk for Psychotic, Bipolar, or Borderline Personality Disorders
official: Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial of a Transdiagnostic, Modular Intervention for Youth at Risk for Psychotic, Bipolar, or Borderline Personality Disorders
summary:
Mental disorders constitute a major challenge to both society, patients and science. Serious mental illnesses (SMIs), such as schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, depression and personality disorders, comprise some of the largest disease burdens worldwide, with no evidence of reduction in recent decades. A range of psycho-social and pharmacological interventions have demonstrated efficacy for improving symptomatic and functional outcomes of SMIs albeit with modest effect sizes and the development of novel, more effective treatments has largely stalled despite a significant number of patients will not respond to treatments. Additionally, there are substantial shortages in access to treatments as well as various barriers, such as perceived need for care and stigma surrounding mental health problems. The planned study aimed to develop and evaluate a novel modular, transdiagnostic psychotherapeutic intervention in n=130 youths at-risk for SMIs. The planned randomized controlled study compares the new developed intervention to TAU in five different study centres.

The Objective is to evaluate the modular, transdiagnostic CBT (AIM-Youth) approach for youths at-risk for SMIs compared to treatment as usual (TAU). Measurements take place as baseline, mid-treatment (3 month), post-treatment (6 month) and follow-up (12-48 month). The primary outcome measure will be psychological distress as measured by the CORE-10 at the end of treatment, secondary outcomes will be CHR-symptoms, quality of life, functioning as well as use of mental health resources at post and follow-up assessment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Participants from a total of three high-risk groups will be included (psychosis, borderline personality disorder, bipolar disorder)

General criteria (All criteria must be met):

* Written consent from the participant (Written consent from legal guardians for minor participants)
* Age: 12 through 35 years old (at the time of enrolment)
* Availability for psychotherapy (once a week)
* German-speaking,
* Participation in the overall cohort of the ECYM cohort

Specific criteria for psychosis (at least ONE criterion)

* At least one SIPS symptom P1-P5 with a score of 3-5 AND a total score ≥ 10
* At least one SIPS symptom P1-P5 with a score of 3-5 OR a first-degree relative with a psychotic disorder AND ≥ 30% decrease in premorbid GAF score
* At least one SIPS symptom P1-P5 with a score of 6

Specific criteria for bipolar disorder (At least ONE criterion)

* BPSS: M1 with a score of ≥ 3 AND ≥ 2 symptoms M3-M10 with a score of ≥ 3 (M7 and M9 count as one symptom)
* BPSS: M2 with a score of ≥ 3 AND ≥ 3 symptoms from M3-M10 with a score of ≥ 3 (M7 and M9 count as one symptom)

Specific Criteria for Borderline Personality Disorder

• At least three symptoms but fewer than 5 criteria from the SCID-5-PD over a period of at least 1 year

Exclusion Criteria:

Patients will be excluded if:

* Presence of schizophrenia, schizotypal disorder, or delusional disorder (ICD-10: F2)
* Mental and behavioral disorders due to psychotropic substances (ICD-10: F10-F19) with withdrawal syndrome with delirium (ICD-10: F1x.4), psychotic disorder (ICD-10: F1x.5), or residual state/delayed-onset psychotic disorder (ICD-10: F1x.7)
* Presence of mania (ICD-10: F30), bipolar affective disorder (ICD-10: F31.x) or major depressive episode with psychotic symptoms (ICD-10: F32.3)
* Presence of a personality disorder, including borderline personality disorder (n.A. for CHR-BP, ICD-10: F60-F69)
* Neurological, neuroendocrine, or other medical conditions with possible causal relevance to psychotic symptoms
* IQ \< 70
* Ongoing outpatient treatment or inpatient hospitalization (at the time of enrolment)
